bio: Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed ( el-SAY-id; born October 31, 1984) is an American politician, epidemiologist, and academic who is the United States senator-elect from Michigan.

items.t: Supports stronger enforcement of anti-monopoly laws and the elimination of corporate tax breaks.
items.q: advocating for stronger enforcement of anti-monopoly laws and the elimination of corporate tax breaks

items.t: Supports regulating billionaires to fund public infrastructure.
items.q: He has said that regulating billionaires to fund public infrastructure is "not that radical"

items.t: Supports repealing Michigan state laws that block local governments from levying a municipal sales tax or enacting rent control laws (2018).
items.q: In 2018, El-Sayed supported repealing Michigan state laws that block local governments from levying a municipal sales tax or enacting rent control laws.

items.t: Supports abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) while also supporting securing the Mexico–United States border.
items.q: El-Sayed supports abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), arguing that it no longer functions as a legitimate law enforcement agency.

items.t: Supports Medicare for All and co-authored a book on the topic.
items.q: He supports Medicare for All and co-authored a book on the topic.

items.t: Supports tougher enforcement of environmental laws and achieving 100% renewable energy in Michigan by 2030.
items.q: has called for tougher enforcement of environmental laws and for merging Michigan's Department of Natural Resources and the Department of Environmental Quality into a single "Department of the Environment", and achieving 100% renewable energy in Michigan by 2030.

items.t: Called for guarantees that data center operation will not result in rate increases passed on to customers.
items.q: He has called for guarantees that the operation of data centers will not result in rate increases passed on to customers.

items.t: His 2026 platform calls for funding police recruitment, retention, and retirement; his campaign says he does not support defunding the police.
items.q: his Senate campaign has said he does not support defunding the police; his 2026 platform calls for funding police recruitment, retention, and retirement.

items.t: Said the US should not fund foreign militaries in Israel, Egypt, Jordan, and Saudi Arabia (2026).
items.q: In 2026, El-Sayed said the US should not fund foreign militaries in Israel, Egypt, Jordan, and Saudi Arabia.

items.t: Called the 2026 Iran war illegal and is against U.S. military intervention to overthrow the Iranian government.
items.q: He called the war illegal and said it did not increase American security

items.t: Called the Russo-Ukrainian war a war between democracy and autocracy (2022).
items.q: called the Russo-Ukrainian war "a war between democracy and autocracy, between self-government and fascism"

items.t: Called for ending all unconditional U.S. military aid to Israel.
items.q: called for ending all unconditional U.S. military aid to Israel.

items.t: Called the war in the Gaza Strip a genocide and called for a ceasefire (January 2024).
items.q: On a January 2024 podcast, El-Sayed called the war in the Gaza Strip a genocide and called for a ceasefire.

items.t: Said he recognizes Israel's right to exist and supports self-determination for Palestinians and Jewish Israelis alike.
items.q: El-Sayed supports "self-determination for Palestinians and Jewish Israelis alike".

items.t: Supports constitutional protections for religious freedom under the First Amendment.
items.q: El-Sayed has expressed support for constitutional protections for religious freedom under the First Amendment.

items.t: Released a plan calling for more regulation of artificial intelligence and opposing new data center approvals until federal safeguards are established (June 2026).
items.q: In June 2026, El-Sayed released a plan calling for more regulation of artificial intelligence and opposed the approval of new data centers until federal safeguards are established.

items.t: Supports unionization and the Protecting the Right to Organize Act.
items.q: He has expressed support for the Protecting the Right to Organize Act alongside unionization efforts among further professions, such as physicians.

items.t: Has vowed not to accept PAC donations, accepting donations from individuals only.
